w: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
k: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:

w: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
k: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.

w: Give us today our daily bread.
k: Give us this day our daily bread.

w: In praying, don’t use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.
k: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.

w: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.
k: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.

w: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
k: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.

w: Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
k: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.

w: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
k: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.

w: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
k: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.

w: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
k: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

w: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
k: Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?

w: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.
k: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

w: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
k: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.

w: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
k: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?

w: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
k: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?

w: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;
k: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

w: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
k: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.

w: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
k: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

w: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
k: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

w: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
k: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

w: “Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment
to his lifespan?
k: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?

w: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
k: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.

w: But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does,
k: But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth:

w: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
k: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?

w: But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
k: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

w: But you, when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face;
k: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face;

w: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
k: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!

w: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
k: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:

w: Therefore when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may get glory from men. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
k: Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

w: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
k: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

w: so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
k: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.

w: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
k: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

w: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
k: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

w: so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
k: That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.

w: Most certainly I tell you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.
k: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

w: Rather, go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
k: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

w: For I came to set a man at odds against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
k: For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.

w: But whoever denies me before men, him I will also deny before my Father who is in heaven.
k: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.

w: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers,
and cast out demons. Freely you received, so freely give.
k: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.

w: He who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and he who loves son or daughter more than me isn’t worthy of me.
k: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

w: Whoever doesn’t receive you, nor hear your words, as you go out of that house or that city, shake the dust off your feet.
k: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.

w: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you.
k: But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues;

w: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
k: For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.

w: “Behold, I send you out as sheep among wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
k: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.

w: He who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. He who receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.
k: He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward.

w: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.
k: What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops.

w: As you enter into the household, greet it.
k: And when ye come into an house, salute it.

w: But when they deliver you up, don’t be anxious how or what you will say, for it will be given you in that hour what you will say.
k: But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak.

w: “A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.
k: The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord.

w: Therefore don’t be afraid of them, for there is nothing covered that will not be revealed; and hidden that will not be known.
k: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.

w: Whoever gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, most certainly I tell you he will in no way lose his reward.”
k: And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.

w: Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, him I will also confess before my Father who is in heaven.
k: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.

w: He who seeks his life will lose it; and he who loses his life for my sake will find it.
k: He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.

w: “Aren’t two sparrows sold for an assarion coin?
Not one of them falls on the ground apart from your Father’s will,
k: Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.

w: If the household is worthy, let your peace come on it, but if it isn’t worthy, let your peace return to you.
k: And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you.

w: Don’t take any gold, silver, or brass in your money belts.
k: Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses,

w: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next, for most certainly I tell you, you will not have gone through the cities of Israel, until the Son of Man has come.
k: But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.

w: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.
k: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.

w: Yes, and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the nations.
k: And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.

w: Into whatever city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy; and stay there until you go on.
k: And into whatsoever city or town ye shall enter, enquire who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go thence.

w: He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me.
k: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.

w: “Don’t go among the Gentiles, and don’t enter into any city of the Samaritans.
k: Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not:

w: He who doesn’t take his cross and follow after me, isn’t worthy of me.
k: And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.

w: Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
k: Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.

w: “Don’t think that I came to send peace on the earth. I didn’t come to send peace, but a sword.
k: Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword.

w: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
k: And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death.

w: Don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul. Rather, fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
k: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

w: Take no bag for your journey, neither two coats, nor shoes, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.
k: Nor scrip for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves: for the workman is worthy of his meat.

w: It is enough for the disciple that he be like his teacher, and the servant like his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul,
how much more those of his household!
k: It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household?

w: but the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
k: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

w: As you go, preach, saying, ‘The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!’
k: And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.

w: A man’s foes will be those of his own household.
k: And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.

w: By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
k: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

w: “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
k: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

w: Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’
k: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

w: Many will tell me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’
k: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?

w: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
k: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

w: Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven; but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
k: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.

w: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it fell—and great was its fall.”
k: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.

w: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.
k: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

w: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
k: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

w: “Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter in by it.
k: Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:

w: Therefore by their fruits you will know them.
k: Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.

w: A good tree can’t produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree produce good fruit.
k: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

w: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
k: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

w: How
narrow is the gate, and restricted is the way that leads to life! Few are those who find it.
k: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.

w: You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
k: Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.

w: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.
k: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:

w: Even so, every good tree produces good fruit; but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit.
k: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

w: Or who is there among you, who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
k: Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone?

w: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
k: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

w: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
k: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

w: Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye;’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?
k: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye?

w: For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
k: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.

w: Everyone who hears these words of mine, and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man, who built his house on the sand.
k: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand:

w: Therefore whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
k: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

w: Every tree that doesn’t grow good fruit is cut down, and thrown into the fire.
k: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

w: “Don’t give that which is holy to the dogs, neither throw your pearls before the pigs, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
k: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.

w: Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent?
k: Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?

w: When evening had come, the lord of the vineyard said to his manager, ‘Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last to the first.’
k: So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.

w: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, to scourge, and to crucify; and the third day he will be raised up.”
k: And shall deliver him to the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify him: and the third day he shall rise again.

w: even as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
k: Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

w: So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”
k: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.

w: When the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise each received a denarius.
k: But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more; and they likewise received every man a penny.

w: It shall not be so among you, but whoever desires to become great among you shall be
your servant.
k: But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;

w: When he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius
a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
k: And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

w: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,
k: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be betrayed unto the chief priests and unto the scribes, and they shall condemn him to death,

w: Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour,
and did likewise.
k: Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise.

w: “You will indeed drink my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with, but to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give; but it is for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”
k: Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.

w: “What do you want?”
k: What wilt thou?

w: When they received it, they murmured against the master of the household,
k: And when they had received it, they murmured against the goodman of the house,

w: Whoever desires to be first among you shall be your bondservant,
k: And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant:

w: He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.’ So they went their way.
k: And said unto them; Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way.

w: Isn’t it lawful for me to do what I want to with what I own? Or is your eye evil, because I am good?’
k: Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?

w: “What do you want me to do for you?”
k: What will ye that I shall do unto you?

w: He went out about the third hour,
and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.
k: And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace,

w: “When those who were hired at about the eleventh hour came, they each received a denarius.
k: And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny.

w: “But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?
k: But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a penny?

w: About the eleventh hour
he went out, and found others standing idle. He said to them, ‘Why do you stand here all day idle?’
k: And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing idle, and saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?

w: “For the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who was the master of a household, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.
k: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.

w: Take that which is yours, and go your way. It is my desire to give to this last just as much as to you.
k: Take that thine is, and go thy way: I will give unto this last, even as unto thee.

w: saying, ‘These last have spent one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!’
k: Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.

w: “You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
k: Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.

w: “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”
k: Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?

w: “They said to him, ‘Because no one has hired us.’
“He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and you will receive whatever is right.’
k: They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard; and whatsoever is right, that shall ye receive.

w: Which of the two did the will of his father?”
“Most certainly I tell you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering into God’s Kingdom before you.
k: Whether of them twain did the will of his father? Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.

w: “Yes. Did you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of babes and nursing babies you have perfected praise?’”
k: Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?

w: He answered, ‘I will not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and went.
k: He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.

w: “It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer,’
but you have made it a den of robbers!”
k: It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

w: So they took him, and threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
k: And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.

w: He came to the second, and said the same thing. He answered, ‘I’ m going, sir,’ but he didn’t go.
k: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.

w: “Most certainly I tell you, if you have faith, and don’t doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you told this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ it would be done.
k: Verily I say unto you, If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do this which is done to the fig tree, but also if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; it shall be done.

w: “Let there be no fruit from you forever!”
k: Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever.

w: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. When you saw it, you didn’t even repent afterward, that you might believe him.
k: For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.

w: All things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive.”
k: And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.

w: “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.
k: Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

w: “I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.
k: I also will ask you one thing, which if ye tell me, I in like wise will tell you by what authority I do these things.

w: But afterward he sent to them his son, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
k: But last of all he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.

w: “Did you never read in the Scriptures,
‘The stone which the builders rejected,
the same was made the head of the corner.
This was from the Lord.
It is marvelous in our eyes?’
k: Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes?

w: “Therefore I tell you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you, and will be given to a nation producing its fruit.
k: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.

w: When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”
k: When the lord therefore of the vineyard cometh, what will he do unto those husbandmen?

w: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but on whomever it will fall, it will scatter him as dust.”
k: And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.

w: When the season for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the farmers, to receive his fruit.
k: And when the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, that they might receive the fruits of it.

w: But the farmers, when they saw the son, said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him, and seize his inheritance.’
k: But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance.

w: “Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them, and bring them to me.
k: Go into the village over against you, and straightway ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me.

w: But what do you think? A man had two sons, and he came to the first, and said, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’
k: But what think ye? A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard.

w: The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?”
k: The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or of men?

w: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they treated them the same way.
k: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they did unto them likewise.

w: “Hear another parable. There was a man who was a master of a household, who planted a vineyard, set a hedge about it, dug a wine press in it, built a tower, leased it out to farmers, and went into another country.
k: Hear another parable: There was a certain householder, which planted a vineyard, and hedged it round about, and digged a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country:

w: The farmers took his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
k: And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.

w: If anyone says anything to you, you shall say, ‘The Lord needs them,’ and immediately he will send them.”
k: And if any man say ought unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and straightway he will send them.

w: But because he couldn’t pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
k: But forasmuch as he had not to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.

w: “Woe to the world because of occasions of stumbling! For it must be that the occasions come, but woe to that person through whom the occasion comes!
k: Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!

w: “But that servant went out, and found one of his fellow servants, who owed him one hundred denarii,
and he grabbed him, and took him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe!’
k: But the same servant went out, and found one of his fellowservants, which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that thou owest.

w: If he finds it, most certainly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which have not gone astray.
k: And if so be that he find it, verily I say unto you, he rejoiceth more of that sheep, than of the ninety and nine which went not astray.

w: “So his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you!’
k: And his fellowservant fell down at his feet, and besought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.

w: His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors, until he should pay all that was due to him.
k: And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due unto him.

w: So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don’t each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.”
k: So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.

w: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
k: Even so it is not the will of your Father which is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.

w: but whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him that a huge millstone should be hung around his neck, and that he should be sunk in the depths of the sea.
k: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.

w: Whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me,
k: And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.

w: “Most certainly I tell you, unless you turn, and become as little children, you will in no way enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
k: Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

w: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. If he refuses to hear the assembly also, let him be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector.
k: And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.

w: The servant therefore fell down and knelt before him, saying, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you all!’
k: The servant therefore fell down, and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.

w: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”
k: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.

w: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.
k: Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.

w: For the Son of Man came to save that which was lost.
k: For the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.

w: Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’
k: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?

w: Therefore the Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king, who wanted to reconcile accounts with his servants.
k: Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, which would take account of his servants.

w: “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.
k: I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.

w: “What do you think? If a man has one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine, go to the mountains, and seek that which has gone astray?
k: How think ye? if a man have an hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and goeth into the mountains, and seeketh that which is gone astray?

w: See that you don’t despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.
k: Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.

w: If your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna
of fire.
k: And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire.

w: The lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt.
k: Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.

w: Then his lord called him in, and said to him, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt, because you begged me.
k: Then his lord, after that he had called him, said unto him, O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me:

w: If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life maimed or crippled, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.
k: Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life halt or maimed, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire.

w: So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were exceedingly sorry, and came and told their lord all that was done.
k: So when his fellowservants saw what was done, they were very sorry, and came and told unto their lord all that was done.

w: Most certainly I tell you, whatever things you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever things you release on earth will have been released in heaven.
k: Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

w: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
k: Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.

w: He would not, but went and cast him into prison, until he should pay back that which was due.
k: And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt.

w: When he had begun to reconcile, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.
k: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, which owed him ten thousand talents.

w: Whoever therefore humbles himself as this little child, the same is the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.
k: Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

w: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
k: But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.

w: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness,
for they shall be filled.
k: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.

w: that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
k: That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.

w: but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.
k: But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.

w: “You are the salt of the earth, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be salted? It is then good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under the feet of men.
k: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.

w: Blessed are those who mourn,
for they shall be comforted.
k: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

w: Blessed are the peacemakers,
for they shall be called children of God.
k: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

w: You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden.
k: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.

w: “If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has anything against you,
k: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee;

w: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor
and hate your enemy.’
k: Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.

w: But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.
k: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

w: “Again you have heard that it was said to them of old time, ‘You shall not make false vows, but shall perform to the Lord your vows,’
k: Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:

w: Whoever, therefore, shall break one of these least commandments, and teach others to do so, shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whoever shall do and teach them shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.
k: Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.

w: If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
k: And if thy right hand offend thee, cut if off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.

w: Blessed are the merciful,
for they shall obtain mercy.
k: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.

w: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake,
for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
k: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

w: “Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill.
k: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.

w: “It was also said, ‘Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorce,’
k: It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:

w: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
k: For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?

w: leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
k: Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.

w: Agree with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way; lest perhaps the prosecutor deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison.
k: Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.

w: but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
k: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne:

w: “You have heard that it was said,
‘You shall not commit adultery;’
k: Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery:

w: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
k: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

w: “You have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not murder;’
and ‘Whoever murders will be in danger of the judgment.’
k: Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment:

w: If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also.
k: And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also.

w: For most certainly, I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not even one smallest letter
or one tiny pen stroke
shall in any way pass away from the law, until all things are accomplished.
k: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.

w: But I tell you, that everyone who is angry with his brother without a cause
will be in danger of the judgment; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca!’
will be in danger of the council; and whoever says, ‘You fool!’ will be in danger of the fire of Gehenna.
k: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.

w: Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.
k: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

w: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, there is no way you will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
k: For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.

w: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
k: But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

w: Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house.
k: Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.

w: If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors
do the same?
k: And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the publicans so?

w: “Blessed are the poor in spirit,
for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
k: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

w: Blessed are the pure in heart,
for they shall see God.
k: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.

w: Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
k: And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain.

w: but I tell you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries her when she is put away commits adultery.
k: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery.

w: “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
k: Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:

w: Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
k: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

w: Neither shall you swear by your head, for you can’t make one hair white or black.
k: Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.

w: Most certainly I tell you, you shall by no means get out of there, until you have paid the last penny.
k: Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou hast paid the uttermost farthing.

w: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
k: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King.

w: Rejoice, and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven. For that is how they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
k: Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.

w: Blessed are the gentle,
for they shall inherit the earth.
k: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.

w: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
k: And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.

w: “Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
k: Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.

w: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.
k: Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.

w: “You said it.”
k: Thou hast said.

w: For you always have the poor with you; but you don’t always have me.
k: For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.

w: “Most certainly I tell you that tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
k: Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

w: Or do you think that I couldn’t ask my Father, and he would even now send me more than twelve legions of angels?
k: Thinkest thou that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels?

w: “Go into the city to a certain person, and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is at hand. I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.”’”
k: Go into the city to such a man, and say unto him, The Master saith, My time is at hand; I will keep the passover at thy house with my disciples.

w: “Most certainly I tell you that one of you will betray me.”
k: Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.

w: Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
k: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

w: “What, couldn’t you watch with me for one hour?
k: And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?

w: “You have said it. Nevertheless, I tell you, after this you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming on the clouds of the sky.”
k: Thou hast said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.

w: “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
k: All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.

w: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be spoken of as a memorial of her.”
k: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, there shall also this, that this woman hath done, be told for a memorial of her.

w: “You know that after two days the Passover is coming, and the Son of Man will be delivered up to be crucified.”
k: Ye know that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.

w: “Sit here, while I go there and pray.”
k: Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder.

w: “My Father, if this cup can’t pass away from me unless I drink it, your desire be done.”
k: O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.

w: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
k: Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

w: “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
k: O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.

w: “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here, and watch with me.”
k: My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me.

w: Arise, let’s be going. Behold, he who betrays me is at hand.”
k: Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me.

w: “Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me? I sat daily in the temple teaching, and you didn’t arrest me.
k: Are ye come out as against a thief with swords and staves for to take me? I sat daily with you teaching in the temple, and ye laid no hold on me.

w: “Friend, why are you here?”
k: Friend, wherefore art thou come?

w: “Take, eat; this is my body.”
k: Take, eat; this is my body.

w: For in pouring this ointment on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.
k: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial.

w: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that it must be so?”
k: But how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be?

w: “He who dipped his hand with me in the dish, the same will betray me.
k: He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me.

w: The Son of Man goes, even as it is written of him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
k: The Son of man goeth as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born.

w: But after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.”
k: But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.

w: “Why do you trouble the woman? She has done a good work for me.
k: Why trouble ye the woman? for she hath wrought a good work upon me.

w: “All of you drink it,
k: Drink ye all of it;

w: “Sleep on now, and take your rest. Behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
k: Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

w: “Put your sword back into its place, for all those who take the sword will die by the sword.
k: Put up again thy sword into his place: for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.

w: for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins.
k: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.

w: But all this has happened, that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.”
k: But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.

w: But I tell you that I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it anew with you in my Father’s Kingdom.”
k: But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.

w: “Why do you also disobey the commandment of God because of your tradition?
k: Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition?

w: “Woman, great is your faith! Be it done to you even as you desire.”
k: O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt.

w: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false testimony, and blasphemies.
k: For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:

w: “I wasn’t sent to anyone but the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
k: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

w: These are the things which defile the man; but to eat with unwashed hands doesn’t defile the man.”
k: These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.

w: he shall not honor his father or mother.’ You have made the commandment of God void because of your tradition.
k: And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.

w: “Do you also still not understand?
k: Are ye also yet without understanding?

w: ‘These people draw near to me with their mouth,
and honor me with their lips;
but their heart is far from me.
k: This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.

w: You hypocrites! Well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,
k: Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying,

w: “Every plant which my heavenly Father didn’t plant will be uprooted.
k: Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.

w: And in vain do they worship me,
teaching as doctrine rules made by men.’”
k: But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

w: “I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days and have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them away fasting, or they might faint on the way.”
k: I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat: and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.

w: Don’t you understand that whatever goes into the mouth passes into the belly, and then out of the body?
k: Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?

w: “It is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
k: It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.

w: That which enters into the mouth doesn’t defile the man; but that which proceeds out of the mouth, this defiles the man.”
k: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.

w: But you say, ‘Whoever may tell his father or his mother, “Whatever help you might otherwise have gotten from me is a gift devoted to God,”
k: But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me;

w: For God commanded, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’
and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’
k: For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.

w: Leave them alone. They are blind guides of the blind. If the blind guide the blind, both will fall into a pit.”
k: Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.

w: But the things which proceed out of the mouth come out of the heart, and they defile the man.
k: But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.

w: “How many loaves do you have?”
k: How many loaves have ye?

w: “Hear, and understand.
k: Hear, and understand:

w: No one puts a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch would tear away from the garment, and a worse hole is made.
k: No man putteth a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse.

w: “Make room, because the girl isn’t dead, but sleeping.”
k: Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleepeth.

w: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins-”
“Get up, and take up your mat, and go to your house.”
k: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins,Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.

w: “According to your faith be it done to you.”
k: According to your faith be it unto you.

w: “Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”
k: Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.

w: “Do you believe that I am able to do this?”
k: Believe ye that I am able to do this?

w: “Follow me.”
k: Follow me.

w: But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’
for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
k: But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

w: “Can the friends of the bridegroom mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.
k: Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.

w: “See that no one knows about this.”
k: See that no man know it.

w: For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk?’
k: For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk?

w: “Daughter, cheer up! Your faith has made you well.”
k: Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole.

w: Neither do people put new wine into old wine skins, or else the skins would burst, and the wine be spilled, and the skins ruined. No, they put new wine into fresh wine skins, and both are preserved.”
k: Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.

w: “Why do you think evil in your hearts?
k: Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?

w: Pray therefore that the Lord of the harvest will send out laborers into his harvest.”
k: Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.

w: “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the laborers are few.
k: The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;

w: “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.
k: They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.

w: Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’
k: Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us.

w: When did we see you as a stranger, and take you in; or naked, and clothe you?
k: When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee?

w: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’
k: His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

w: “For it is like a man, going into another country, who called his own servants, and entrusted his goods to them.
k: For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods.

w: for I was hungry, and you didn’t give me food to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink;
k: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink:

w: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten virgins, who took their lamps, and went out to meet the bridegroom.
k: Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.

w: But he answered, ‘Most certainly I tell you, I don’t know you.’
k: But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.

w: Those who were foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them,
k: They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them:

w: You ought therefore to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I should have received back my own with interest.
k: Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.

w: While they went away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was shut.
k: And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.

w: “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers,
you did it to me.’
k: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.

w: Before him all the nations will be gathered, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
k: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:

w: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’
k: His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

w: “But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
k: When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:

w: In the same way, he also who got the two gained another two.
k: And likewise he that had received two, he also gained other two.

w: “He also who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Lord, I knew you that you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow, and gathering where you did not scatter.
k: Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed:

w: Take away therefore the talent from him, and give it to him who has the ten talents.
k: Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents.

w: but the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.
k: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.

w: The foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’
k: And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out.

w: For to everyone who has will be given, and he will have abundance, but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away.
k: For unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath.

w: He will set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.
k: And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.

w: He who received the five talents came and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Lord, you delivered to me five talents. Behold, I have gained another five talents besides them.’
k: And so he that had received five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents: behold, I have gained beside them five talents more.

w: I was a stranger, and you didn’t take me in; naked, and you didn’t clothe me; sick, and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’
k: I was a stranger, and ye took me not in: naked, and ye clothed me not: sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not.

w: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
k: And five of them were wise, and five were foolish.

w: “Then they will also answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and didn’t help you?’
k: Then shall they also answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, or athirst, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister unto thee?

w: But he who received the one talent went away and dug in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.
k: But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.

w: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.
k: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.

w: But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Behold! The bridegroom is coming! Come out to meet him!’
k: And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.

w: These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
k: And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.

w: I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you came to me.’
k: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.

w: “Then he will answer them, saying, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you didn’t do it to one of the least of these, you didn’t do it to me.’
k: Then shall he answer them, saying, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me.

w: “But his lord answered him, ‘You wicked and slothful servant. You knew that I reap where I didn’t sow, and gather where I didn’t scatter.
k: His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed:

w: Now while the bridegroom delayed, they all slumbered and slept.
k: While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept.

w: I was afraid, and went away and hid your talent in the earth. Behold, you have what is yours.’
k: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, there thou hast that is thine.

w: for I was hungry, and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me drink. I was a stranger, and you took me in.
k: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:

w: “Now after a long time the lord of those servants came, and reconciled accounts with them.
k: After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them.

w: Immediately he who received the five talents went and traded with them, and made another five talents.
k: Then he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents.

w: When did we see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?’
k: Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee?

w: Then he will say also to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels;
k: Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:

w: Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
k: Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:

w: Watch therefore, for you don’t know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.
k: Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.

w: “He also who got the two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents. Behold, I have gained another two talents besides them.’
k: He also that had received two talents came and said, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me two talents: behold, I have gained two other talents beside them.

w: “Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, and feed you; or thirsty, and give you a drink?
k: Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink?

w: Throw out the unprofitable servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
k: And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

w: But the wise answered, saying, ‘What if there isn’t enough for us and you? You go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.’
k: But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.

w: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one; to each according to his own ability. Then he went on his journey.
k: And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey.

w: I also tell you that you are Peter,
and on this rock
I will build my assembly, and the gates of Hades
will not prevail against it.
k: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

w: “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, for you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.”
k: Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.

w: “Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?”
k: Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?

w: “Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, ‘because you have brought no bread?’
k: O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves, because ye have brought no bread?

w: I will give to you the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; and whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.”
k: And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

w: “But who do you say that I am?”
k: But whom say ye that I am?

w: Don’t you yet perceive, neither remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
k: Do ye not yet understand, neither remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?

w: For the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will render to everyone according to his deeds.
