k: For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.

w: How is it that you don’t perceive that I didn’t speak to you concerning bread? But beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
k: How is it that ye do not understand that I spake it not to you concerning bread, that ye should beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees?

w: “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
k: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

w: “Blessed are you, Simon Bar Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.
k: Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.

w: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, and whoever will lose his life for my sake will find it.
k: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it.

w: “When it is evening, you say, ‘It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.’
k: When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red.

w: For what will it profit a man, if he gains the whole world, and forfeits his life? Or what will a man give in exchange for his life?
k: For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

w: In the morning, ‘It will be foul weather today, for the sky is red and threatening.’ Hypocrites! You know how to discern the appearance of the sky, but you can’t discern the signs of the times!
k: And in the morning, It will be foul weather to day: for the sky is red and lowring. O ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times?

w: Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste of death, until they see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.”
k: Verily I say unto you, There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.

w: Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you took up?
k: Neither the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?

w: “Take heed and beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
k: Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

w: An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and there will be no sign given to it, except the sign of the prophet Jonah.”
k: A wicked and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given unto it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas.

w: “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
k: With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.

w: “Most certainly I say to you, a rich man will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven with difficulty.
k: Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven.

w: “Not all men can receive this saying, but those to whom it is given.
k: All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given.

w: But many will be last who are first; and first who are last.
k: But many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first.

w: I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and he who marries her when she is divorced commits adultery.”
k: And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.

w: “‘You shall not murder.’ ‘You shall not commit adultery.’ ‘You shall not steal.’ ‘You shall not offer false testimony.’
k: Thou shalt do no murder, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness,

w: For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the Kingdom of Heaven’s sake. He who is able to receive it, let him receive it.”
k: For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven’s sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.

w: “Allow the little children, and don’t forbid them to come to me; for the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to ones like these.”
k: Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

w: Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, will receive one hundred times, and will inherit eternal life.
k: And every one that hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall inherit everlasting life.

w: ‘Honor your father and your mother.’
And, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”
k: Honour thy father and thy mother: and, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

w: “Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
k: Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.

w: and said, ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh?’
k: And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?

w: So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.”
k: Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

w: “Why do you call me good?
No one is good but one, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”
k: Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.

w: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
k: And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

w: “Most certainly I tell you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
k: Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

w: “Haven’t you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female,
k: Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female,

w: “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”
k: If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.

w: Many false prophets will arise, and will lead many astray.
k: And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many.

w: Then many will stumble, and will deliver up one another, and will hate one another.
k: And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.

w: Then two men will be in the field: one will be taken and one will be left.
k: Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.

w: He will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.
k: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.

w: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has set over his household, to give them their food in due season?
k: Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?

w: “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
k: Take heed that no man deceive you.

w: But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven,
but my Father only.
k: But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

w: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and one will be left.
k: Two women shall be grinding at the mill; the one shall be taken, and the other left.

w: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.
k: For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.

w: Blessed is that servant whom his lord finds doing so when he comes.
k: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

w: But he who endures to the end, the same will be saved.
k: But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.

w: and they didn’t know until the flood came, and took them all away, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
k: And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.

w: and will cut him in pieces, and appoint his portion with the hypocrites. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.

w: But all these things are the beginning of birth pains.

k: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.

w: “Behold, I have told you beforehand.
k: Behold, I have told you before.

k: But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.

k: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind:

k: Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.

k: So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares?

w: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast, which a woman took, and hid in three measures

k: The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

Seeing you will see,

k: And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive:

k: And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away.

w: “He said to them, ‘An enemy has done this.’

k: He said unto them, An enemy hath done this. The servants said unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?

k: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.

k: Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.

k: But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it;

w: The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather out of his Kingdom all things that cause stumbling, and those who do iniquity,
k: The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity;

k: Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth:

k: As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world.

k: Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

w: but while people slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel weeds

k: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.

w: The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
k: The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.

w: “Hear, then, the parable of the farmer.
k: Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower.

w: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
k: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

k: Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.

k: But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.

k: And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up:

k: Behold, a sower went forth to sow;

k: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.

k: Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

k: Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift?

k: The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat:

k: And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven.

w: But all their works they do to be seen by men. They make their phylacteries

k: Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!

w: and love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues,

k: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not.

k: Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation.

k: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

k: But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren.

k: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.

w: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin,

k: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.

w: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna

k: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.

w: Therefore you testify to yourselves that you are children of those who killed the prophets.
k: Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.

w: ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it, he is obligated?’
k: And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty.

w: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold?
k: Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold?

k: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.

k: Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

k: Neither be ye called masters: for one is your Master, even Christ.

k: Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith?

w: I tell you that many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven,
k: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.

w: “Go your way. Let it be done for you as you have believed.”
k: Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee.

w: “See that you tell nobody, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
k: See thou tell no man; but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

w: “He who is not with me is against me, and he who doesn’t gather with me, scatters.
k: He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.

w: “Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”
k: Who is my mother? and who are my brethren?

w: The good man out of his good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of his evil treasure
brings out evil things.
k: A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.

w: “Haven’t you read what David did, when he was hungry, and those who were with him;
k: Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him;

w: “What man is there among you, who has one sheep, and if this one falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, won’t he grab on to it, and lift it out?
k: What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?

w: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
k: For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.

w: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, someone greater than Jonah is here.
k: The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

w: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven men.
k: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.

w: Or have you not read in the law, that on the Sabbath day, the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath, and are guiltless?
k: Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless?

w: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age, nor in that which is to come.
k: And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.

w: “Stretch out your hand.”
k: Stretch forth thine hand.

w: Or how can one enter into the house of the strong man, and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.
k: Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.

w: When an unclean spirit has gone out of a man, he passes through waterless places, seeking rest, and doesn’t find it.
k: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none.

w: Then he goes, and takes with himself seven other spirits more evil than he is, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first. Even so will it be also to this evil generation.”
k: Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.

w: “Behold, my mother and my brothers!
k: Behold my mother and my brethren!

w: But if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’
you wouldn’t have condemned the guiltless.
k: But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.

w: “Either make the tree good, and its fruit good, or make the tree corrupt, and its fruit corrupt; for the tree is known by its fruit.
k: Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit.

w: Then he says, ‘I will return into my house from which I came out,’ and when he has come back, he finds it empty, swept, and put in order.
k: Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished.

w: Of how much more value then is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath day.”
k: How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.

w: But I tell you that one greater than the temple is here.
k: But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.

w: If I by Beelzebul cast out demons, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
k: And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.

w: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
k: Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand:

w: how he entered into God’s house, and ate the show bread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for those who were with him, but only for the priests?
k: How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests?

w: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
k: For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.

w: For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.”
k: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.

w: The queen of the south will rise up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, someone greater than Solomon is here.
k: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

w: You offspring of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks.
k: O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.

w: “An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, but no sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.
k: An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas:

w: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.
k: But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you.

w: If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
k: And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand?

w: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
k: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

w: I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment.
k: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.

w: “Rejoice!”
k: All hail.

w: Go
and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
k: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:

w: “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
k: All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.

w: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”
k: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.

w: “Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers
that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me.”
k: Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.

w: “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute? From their children, or from strangers?”
k: What thinkest thou, Simon? of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers?

w: “Faithless and perverse generation! How long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you? Bring him here to me.”
k: O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him hither to me.

w: and they will kill him, and the third day he will be raised up.”
k: And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again.

w: “Get up, and don’t be afraid.”
k: Arise, and be not afraid.

w: “Because of your unbelief. For most certainly I tell you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will tell this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.
k: Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.

w: “The Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men,
k: The Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of men:

w: “Therefore the children are exempt.
k: Then are the children free.

w: “Don’t tell anyone what you saw, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.”
k: Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.

w: But this kind doesn’t go out except by prayer and fasting.”
k: Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.

w: “Elijah indeed comes first, and will restore all things,
k: Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things.

w: but I tell you that Elijah has come already, and they didn’t recognize him, but did to him whatever they wanted to. Even so the Son of Man will also suffer by them.”
k: But I say unto you, That Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them.

w: But, lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take up the first fish that comes up. When you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater coin.
Take that, and give it to them for me and you.”
k: Notwithstanding, lest we should offend them, go thou to the sea, and cast an hook, and take up the fish that first cometh up; and when thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a piece of money: that take, and give unto them for me and thee.

w: “Why do you test me, you hypocrites?
k: Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?

w: The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.”
k: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

w: “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
k: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.

w: and sent out his servants to call those who were invited to the marriage feast, but they would not come.
k: And sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding: and they would not come.

w: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Bind him hand and foot, take him away, and throw him into the outer darkness. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.’
k: Then said the king to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

w: But when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who didn’t have on wedding clothing,
k: And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment:

w: ‘The Lord said to my Lord,
sit on my right hand,
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet?’
k: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool?

w: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king, who made a marriage feast for his son,
k: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son,

w: “Whose is this image and inscription?”
k: Whose is this image and superscription?

w: and he said to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here not wearing wedding clothing?’ He was speechless.
k: And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.

w: “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.
k: Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.

w: This is the first and great commandment.
k: This is the first and great commandment.

w: “How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
k: How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying,

w: “Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding is ready, but those who were invited weren’t worthy.
k: Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy.

w: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise,
k: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise:

w: Those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together as many as they found, both bad and good. The wedding was filled with guests.
k: So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.

w: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
k: And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

w: When the king heard that, he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
k: But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.

w: and the rest grabbed his servants, and treated them shamefully, and killed them.
k: And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them.

w: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,
k: But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying,

w: Again he sent out other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who are invited, “Behold, I have prepared my dinner. My cattle and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the marriage feast!”’
k: Again, he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them which are bidden, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come unto the marriage.

w: Go therefore to the intersections of the highways, and as many as you may find, invite to the marriage feast.’
k: Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.

w: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are like God’s angels in heaven.
k: For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.

w: For many are called, but few chosen.”
k: For many are called, but few are chosen.

w: “Give therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
k: Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.

w: “If then David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”
k: If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?

w: “What do you think of the Christ? Whose son is he?”
k: Saying, What think ye of Christ? whose son is he?

w: ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?’
God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
k: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.

w: Show me the tax money.”
k: Shew me the tribute money.

w: “Allow it now, for this is the fitting way for us to fulfill all righteousness.”
k: Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness.

w: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’
k: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a devil.

w: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.
k: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

w: “But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call to their companions
k: But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the markets, and calling unto their fellows,

w: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
k: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

w: and say, ‘We played the flute for you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned for you, and you didn’t lament.’
k: And saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned unto you, and ye have not lamented.

w: All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows the Son, except the Father; neither does anyone know the Father, except the Son, and he to whom the Son desires to reveal him.
k: All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him

w: From the days of John the Baptizer until now, the Kingdom of Heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force.
k: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.

w: You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, you will go down to Hades.
For if the mighty works had been done in Sodom which were done in you, it would have remained until today.
k: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.

w: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
k: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

w: “Go and tell John the things which you hear and see:
k: Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:

w: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is justified by her children.”
k: The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.

w: “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to infants.
k: I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.

w: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
k: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

w: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
k: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

w: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear,
the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.
k: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.

w: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
k: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.

w: But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.
k: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet.

w: But what did you go out to see? A man in soft clothing? Behold, those who wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.
k: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.

w: Most certainly I tell you, among those who are born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptizer; yet he who is least in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he.
k: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

w: For this is he, of whom it is written, ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’
k: For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

w: If you are willing to receive it, this is Elijah, who is to come.
k: And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.

w: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
k: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

w: Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.
k: Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in thy sight.

w: But I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
k: But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.

w: But I tell you that it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom, on the day of judgment, than for you.”
k: But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.

w: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
k: What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?

w: “Again, it is written, ‘You shall not test the Lord, your God.’”
k: It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.

w: “Repent! For the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.”
k: Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

w: “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.’”
k: It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.

w: “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”
k: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

w: “Get behind me,
Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’”
k: Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

w: “Bring them here to me.”
k: Bring them hither to me.

w: “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
k: O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?

w: “Come!”
k: Come.

w: “They don’t need to go away. You give them something to eat.”
k: They need not depart; give ye them to eat.

w: “Cheer up! It is I!
Don’t be afraid.”
k: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.

w: “Eli, Eli, lima
sabachthani?”
“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
k: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

w: “So you say.”
k: Thou sayest.
